subject: Weekly MAP — performance benchmarking checkpoint (latency & throughput)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Tan <lisa.tan@acme-health.com>, Mike O'Neill <mike.oneill@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Weekly MAP — performance benchmarking checkpoint (latency & throughput)

Hi Lisa / Mike,

Attached is the MAP v3 (section: performance validation) and the raw benchmarking CSV from yesterday's run. This week's checkpoint focused on the P95 latency regression you flagged and whether the dedicated routing profile reduces tail latency during synthetic peak bursts.

Key summary up front:
- Baseline (last week, hosted): p50=210ms, p95=920ms, throughput=320 req/s
- Yesterday's dedicated run (same model, optimized kernels): p50=180ms, p95=1.15s, throughput=540 req/s
- Observed spike window between 14:20–14:35 where p95 jumped to ~2.8–3.4s on a subset of requests that contain long system prompts

As discussed in the MAP, we want to:
1) Triage the spike root cause (KV-cache miss pattern vs. batching cliff) — owner: Rishi (ETA: 48h)
2) Run a quantization A/B on the dedicated pool for the high-throughput route — owner: Karthik (ETA: next run, 72h)
3) Update MAP close timeline to keep March 31 as target but flag a contingency for a 1-week slip if we need additional evals — owner: Jonas (ETA: update today)

Please review the attached CSV and the notes in section 3 of the MAP (link below). If you have internal perf traces you can share, please attach them and we will correlate with our server-side traces.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sync Friday 10:00 PT to walk the spike traces and agree next week’s gating criteria for cutover.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0119

Attachments: acme_map_v3.pdf (MAP with success criteria), benchmark-results-20260314.csv (raw), kv-cache-heatmap.png

From: Lisa Tan <lisa.tan@acme-health.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike O'Neill <mike.oneill@acme-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP — performance benchmarking checkpoint (latency & throughput)

Thanks Jonas — good summary. I forwarded the CSV to our infra team and they returned initial traces: they see the same spike window and it correlates with a small percentage of calls (~1.6%) that include a 7k token system prompt followed by a multi-turn user context. Their note: these requests bypassed our client-side prefix caching due to a tokenization mismatch on our side. I'm attaching the Acme perf trace and a short note from our infra lead.

Preliminary asks from Acme:
- Can Redwood run the same dedicated profile but with relaxed max-batch-wait (lower to 5ms) to see if it reduces the spike?
- We want a mapping of request size -> expected p95 for the dedicated pool (so our client router can split routes)

We remain aligned on the March 31 target but will expect documented gating criteria before cutover (p95 < 1.0s for 99% of typical request mix).

Lisa Tan
Director of Platform — Acme Health
lisa.tan@acme-health.com

Attachments: acme-infra-trace-20260314.json

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Tan <lisa.tan@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP — performance benchmarking checkpoint (latency & throughput)

Quick coordination note and proposed owner cadence for the MAP row "Performance validation":

Action items (owners & short notes):
- Rishi: run KV-cache instrumentation and correlate with client trace (Acme infra) — deliverable: annotated traces + hypothesis (48h)
- Karthik: spin a quantization A/B on dedicated pool (q8_0 vs q4_0) to measure p95 delta and throughput change — deliverable: A/B report (72h)
- Marissa: update MAP v3 with a gating checklist and revised cutover plan (if we see persistent spikes) — deliverable: MAP v3.1 (EOD Monday)
- Jonas: coordinate Friday sync invite and confirm stakeholders (done after this thread) — deliverable: calendar invite (today)

Notes:
- For the gating checklist I propose three pass/fail items: 1) p95 <= 1.0s for canonical workload, 2) no single-request tail > 3s more than 0.5% of runs, 3) throughput within 85% of target under simulated burst.
- If the A/B shows quantization reduces p95 at cost of lower sample quality, we will include a quality regression check (prompt-set from MAP section 5).

I'll start the MAP doc update and will drop the section link here once published to the shared Drive.

-Marissa
Product Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Tan <lisa.tan@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP — performance benchmarking checkpoint (latency & throughput)

Acknowledged — starting KV-cache instrumentation now. Quick notes from infra:
- Hypothesis: the spike is a cache miss amplification when long system prompts exceed the inline prefix cache cutoff. We'll validate by forcing a warm-prefix run and comparing p95.
- I'll also capture per-batch tokenization/parsing time to ensure we aren't CPU-bound on tokenization for the long prompts.
- If the miss amplification is confirmed, short-term mitigation: temporary route-level prefix-preserve flag for Acme's dedicated pool (can be enabled within one business day). Long-term: recommend client-side canonical tokenization + a small server-side prefix cache extension.

I'll upload the annotated traces to the Drive link and ping when done.

-Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

- Marissa: MAP v3.1 with gating checklist (ETA: EOD Monday)

I'll mark the MAP row as "In progress — active validation" and will push an updated ETA in the HubSpot deal once the 48h run results land.

See you Friday.

Jonas
